title: Candidate goal: let a draughtsman lay out a double-line wall by picking its centreline chain

behaviour.statement: C:Wall-Dline turns an interactively picked point chain into two parallel LINE chains offset w1=10 and w2=20 perpendicular to each segment, extended to infinite-line intersections at each direction change, one LINE entity per segment (see rule record C4L-WAL-01).
behaviour.note: Static readings only; no recorded run of C:Wall-Dline exists (probe velisp-002 covers geom.lisp kernels, not wall.lisp; execution unverified). Evidence list is deliberately sparse: LLCO goal records are evidence-limited.

evidence.detail: Widths hardcoded w1 10 / w2 20 at src/wall.lisp:65; offsets via polar +/- pi/2 (segxlist, 93-113); mitres via (inters ... nil) extended form (intlst, 116-138); two vertex chains handed to Geom-EntmakeLines (170-171).
Commented-out Geom-EntmakexPolyline calls at wall.lisp:168-169 above the active Geom-EntmakeLines calls at 170-171: the author's own record of switching LWPOLYLINE output to separate LINE entities.

purpose.statement: Candidate (ai_generated): C:Wall-Dline exists so a draughtsman can produce plan linework for both faces of a wall quickly and consistently, instead of hand-drawing parallel wall lines. Beneficiary: the draughtsman producing plans.
purpose.note: Supporting evidence only. No named process owner exists for this public development-alpha library, so the purpose cannot be confirmed under the human-authority rule (LOG-0023); it stays a candidate.

evidence.detail: Interactive chain entry with live grdraw preview and immediate geometry output indicates a drafting-speed tool, not a data exchange.
'set the wall width' prompt string (wall.lisp:64) shows production use with variable widths was intended, i.e. a real drawing task rather than a demo.

correctness.statement: Unknown whether 10/20-unit double lines are the correct wall representation for any process: no specification, standard or QA record exists in the repository.
correctness.note: No governing document; nothing to evaluate against.

authority.basis_note: Rule record C4L-WAL-01 claims drafting_habit (no comment or document states a firm convention; the two widths are unexplained constants). Mapped per the USG proposal's mapping table: drafting habit -> preference or assumption; recorded as assumption, relaxable by the estate owner.

concerns.statement: The plan shows both wall faces as two parallel line chains, offset asymmetrically (10 / 20 drawing units) from the picked chain, mitred at each change of direction.
The picked chain is entered interactively with a live preview; the two widths are fixed constants in this version.
Geometry is emitted as separate LINE entities via entmake, one per segment, not a polyline.
Corners are computed as infinite-line intersections of adjacent offset segments (inters extended form).

required_outputs: plan linework representing both wall faces for every wall in the chain

coverage.what: Producing double-line wall geometry from an interactively picked chain.
coverage.reason: Candidate native coverage in a BIM successor (wall objects model wall geometry directly) is NOT claimed: no versioned primary-source evidence has been recorded, the estate has no process owner to rule the purpose, and a successor target has not been selected. Blocked pending both.

evidence.detail: Coverage assessment impossible beyond code structure; see rule record C4L-WAL-01 for the kernel reading.

coverage.what: The separate-LINE / entmake output representation and the interactive grdraw preview.
coverage.reason: Looks like platform mechanism / era constraint (candidate retire in a successor), but retirement would follow only after the purpose ruling and successor selection; not decided here.
